Q: Scoring items if the text appears in another list A:

COUNTIFS() will give you direct count of founded records. Try =COUNTIFS(E:E,A2). If you just need 0 and 1 then try =--ISNUMBER(MATCH(A2,E:E,0)).

Q: SELECT accounts which logged in at least once per month since registering with MySQL A:

Another solution could be use the same table again with an alias

SELECT DISTINCT lh1.player_id 
FROM login_history lh1 join login_history lh2 on lh1.player_id  = lh2.player_id 
WHERE lh1.timestamp BETWEEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-01-01 00:00:00') 
AND (UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-02-01 00:00:00')-1) 
AND lh2.timestamp BETWEEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-02-01 00:00:00') 
AND (UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-03-01 00:00:00')-1);

If the number of rows is too high you can use subqueries

SELECT DISTINCT lh1.player_id 
FROM 
(Select distinct player_id from login_history 
WHERE lh1.timestamp BETWEEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-01-01 00:00:00') 
AND (UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-02-01 00:00:00')-1) )lh1 
JOIN
(Select distinct player_id from login_history 
WHERE lh2.timestamp BETWEEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-02-01 00:00:00') 
AND (UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2014-03-01 00:00:00')-1) )lh2 on lh1.player_id  = lh2.player_id;

Hopes it helps. Regards.

Q: Accessing jasper reports through the web A:

The topic is old, but I’m leaving this note for anyone still looking for a lightweight way to view reports on the web.

You don't necessarily need JasperReports Server (which is a commerical product now) for rendering reports as html. You can fill the report and then export it as HTML through JasperReports Library APIs. Interactivity like drill downs and pagination requires some effort but for simple reports, you can embed images and charts and render the HTML in an iframe.

Basically using JasperFillManager for filling and JasperExportManager for exporting.

After implementing this manually in several Spring Boot apps, we eventually bundled our logic into a reusable SDK/framework to save time. We've just made it available at reportshell.com. It’s a commercial tool, but it's free to use for development and evaluation. If you don't want to purchase it, I think the documentation may still help you implement a similar flow for your own needs. If it is just one app with simple reports and simple parameters, then you don't need any other tool then JR Library at all.

You may also check BIRT Viewer for how they use web APIs for similar stuff. Backend code is of course different but it helps on how to design a web api for report viewers.

Q: Implementing smooth coloring of Mandelbrot set A:

In the demo shading rectangles included with the accepted answer, it will not shade a rectangle with the final color. (first color is pure red, last color is pure blue, so in your demo loop with 10 steps, 0 - 9, step 0 has (255,0,0). That's one step out of num_rects steps.

Step 0 gives you the full first color (0 / 10 * (2) = 0), with iteration mod 0 as your ratio. step through until the 10th step (step 9) and you're at 9 / 10 * (2) = 1.8, mod zero gets your ratio to 0.8, never reaching the full 1.0 ratio.

Depending on the color and number of steps, you might not notice missing the target, and there's not enough room to fit size/rect_count+1 bars in the size square anyway so I added the final step (and a Math.min() since we'll end up over or underflowing when we create c1 or c2 if we just add +1 to rect_count everywhere.

context.fillStyle = interpolation(2.5);
context.fillRect(0, i * (300 / (rect_count + 1)), 300, 300 / (rect_count+1));

The corrected full-range inclusive interpolation forked from the original is at https://jsfiddle.net/x2tmy7v9/1/ where I changed a bit of arithmetic so that it fits the final color in, along with explanatory messages to the debug.console.

Q: trying to import a txt file, read it and then print it. coming up with a crazy error that I dont know what it means A:

UnicodeDecodeError means Python is reading the file with the wrong text encoding.

Your file likely is not being decoded correctly by the default Windows encoding, so specify one explicitly:

with open("0_intro.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as intro_doc:
    print(intro_doc.read())

If that still fails, try encoding="cp1252".

Also, intro_text.close is incorrect:

  • intro_text is a list, not the file

  • close needs parentheses

  • using with open(...) is better because it closes the file automatically

Q: Print the paths of modules and types from command line A:

The two common approaches would be to use cargo doc or trigger a compiler error to see module name in the error message.

cargo doc --open

or introduce a compiler error and do cargo check.

If you want a third party plugin then cargo-modules can be helpful. e.g.,

$ cargo install cargo-modules
$ cargo modules structure

Q: How to get channel description? A:

You can use <channel>.topic for this. For more information, see https://discord.js.org/docs/packages/discord.js/14.26.2/BaseGuildTextChannel:Class#topic
